story.head: Boeser’s favorite opponent
paras: The Canucks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-5 in overtime in Anaheim on Oct 27. The Ducks (5-7-1) lost 7-6 to Buffalo on Thursday, and the Canucks (3-11-1) lost 3-2 to San Jose the same night. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Ducks are sixth in the Pacific (tied for 26th in the NHL) and the Canucks are last in the NHL.

The Ducks’ record (.423) is about what their chances are worth. The Canucks have played better than their record (.233) says: their chances are worth about .299, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Ducks play some of the league’s fastest games (3rd), hit a lot (4th) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (30th). Anaheim has allowed 3.85 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Canucks pick their shots (lowest) and have had shaky goaltending (32nd). They also have a leaky penalty kill (32nd), so the Ducks have the edge over them on the penalty kill. Vancouver has allowed 4.53 goals a game, the most in the league. The Ducks’ forecheck could keep the Canucks pinned in their own end.

Leo Carlsson (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 13 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Beckett Sennecke (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Canucks, Elias Pettersson (#40) (4 G / 12 A / 16 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Jonathan Lekkerimäki (6 G / 6 A / 12 P in 15 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Lukáš Dostál (4-4-1 / .872 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Anaheim, and Leevi Meriläinen (2-4-1 / .898 SV% in 8 GS) for Vancouver.
